messages:
maya: Quick recap: ironclad-7b-int4 int4 bring-up — ran honeypot/persona stress suite. Seeing persona persistence after KV-cache warmup. Repro ~12% (24/200).
sam: omg, 12% is high. baseline fp16 was ~0.5%?
dana: baseline int4 earlier was 0.8% on same suite.
maya: yes, float baseline 0.6%. int4 jump coincides with kvcache enabled + cache_prefetch branch.
eli: can you drop the exact request? headers/params?
maya: pasted curl we used:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
 -d '{"model":"ironclad-7b-int4","prompt":"<HONEYPOT_PROMPT>","kvcache":"enabled","kvcache_warmup":true}'
```
zach: did we accidentally enable a persona-system prompt in the warmup payload?
maya: double-checked — warmup uses canned completions only. but the cached KV seems to carry instruction-like tokens across sessions.
safety-bot: Alert: Possible policy-regression signal — persona leakage detected in 24 samples. Marking severity: medium :warning:
sam: hypothesis: quantization + attention cache packing changed token alignment causing partial system-token bleed. Any kernel changes in last compile?
dana: yes, compiler flagged new fused-attn kernel on 03/15 compile. build id: f-a2b7.
eli: can we reproduce with kv disabled?
maya: repro drops to 0.5% with kvcache off.
zach: ok that's a smoking gun. temp mitigation = disable kvcache for int4 until patch.
sam: can we hot-rollback kvcache flag in staging and run quick smoke?
deploy-bot: deploy queued: staging toggle 'kvcache_enabled' -> false for ironclad-7b-int4 (rollout 100%) by @sam
maya: running 2 quick batches now (200 each).
eli: telemetry: capture token-level traces + prompt/response diffs for the 24 fail cases and 50 random passes. store at: https://playback.redwood/trace/ironclad/1765001234
maya: added notes to eval harness: run_id=irncld-2026-03-15-01
sam: next steps: 1) revert kvcache in staging (in flight) 2) reproduce locally with fused-attn disabled 3) bisect kernel change 4) safety review of leaked outputs
dana: agreed. tagging infra to prioritize. @infra
zach: also want to test int8 and hybrid int4->int8 fallback to see if unit economics worth it for safety.
safety-bot: reminder: escalate to policy if any sensitive content seen. none reported so far.
maya: filed CH ticket: CH-7892 with examples and traces. pinging security + policy.
eli: nice catch, maya. thanks for quick triage :thumbsup:
sam: will follow up with bisect results. keeping this thread for updates.
